transcript.text: Alright everyone, we've got a ten-business-day stability sprint coming up with capacity for one primary technical-debt focus. The three candidates on the table are legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index. Before I lock the plan, I want to do our normal round-robin check-in. Let's start with backend engineering, then security engineering, then customer support — please share your perspective on which candidate you think should be the priority and why.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed. Exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. I haven't updated the planning board yet, but this means legacy_csv_exporter is much closer to completion than it appears on the board.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go further. Minutes ago I confirmed in the dependency scanner that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability. The approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. I was verifying scanner results and haven't filed the security finding yet, but given Devon just indicated legacy_csv_exporter is close to completion and could be finished this sprint, I strongly recommend we prioritize legacy_csv_exporter so we can remediate this vulnerability as part of that work.
transcript.speaker: A3
